Phase 4: blocker review prevents immediate Take and refresh requires a fresh acknowledgment

Phase 4: confirmed second UI activation remains recoverable with isolated development escape
Phase 5: real plugin reload reattaches active ownership without duplicate guards or docks
Phase 5: resume and display events preserve fullscreen and reposition the dock
Phase 5: separate popout cannot acquire a second Strict owner
Phase 5: actual dock renderer crash is reconstructed with the same policy
Phase 5: renderer-loss handling releases guards and records interruption

Phase 5: fresh process recovers a persisted active commitment once without re-entering fullscreen

limitations: Actual plugin reload, dock renderer crash and fresh-process startup were exercised in disposable Obsidian.
Host renderer-loss, power resume and display change events are simulated; physical hardware/OS transitions require manual acceptance.
Synthetic task/workspace/index adapters and fixture-scoped preflight protect ordinary applications and user data.
Physical Alt+Tab, foreground ownership and arbitrary external-window stacking are not asserted by automation.

launcher.source: Installed Obsidian archive in existing test Electron; not the installed launcher runtime
